feedback.end: On the 11th March 2011, a catastrophic earthquake hit Japan.

instruction.text: Read the text and answer the questions.

atoms.text: The earthquake’s epicentre was in the Pacific Ocean, around 80 miles from a city called Sendai. It measured 9 on the Richter scale, making it one of the strongest earthquakes ever recorded.
The earthquake happened on the plate boundary between the Pacific and North American plates, which is an area prone to earthquakes.

Several foreshocks could be felt before the mainshock, including an event measuring 7 on the Richter scale. After the earthquake, over 800 aftershocks hit in the surrounding areas, some of which also measured up to 7.
atoms.sound: Several fore shocks could be felt before the mainshock, including an event measuring 7 on the Richter scale. After the earthquake, over 800 after shocks hit in the surrounding areas, some of which also measured up to 7.

atoms.b: regular earthquake drills, so people knew what to do.

atoms.sound: The Prime Minister put an earthquake plan into action just four minutes after it hit.

feedback.finish: Even though the earthquake was one of the most powerful ever recorded, Japan was well prepared with a sensible plan.

atoms.b: As the earthquake happened in ((space ++the_ocean)), it triggered a powerful tsunami that caused severe damage to coastal regions in East ((China ++Japan)), specifically in a town called Tohoku.
There were a series of large waves, some reaching as high as 10 metres! These waves ((dried_out ++flooded)) multiple towns and cities, causing mass destruction to buildings, cars and roads.
Although Japan was well prepared for the ((++earthquake volcano)), they did not expect the tsunami that followed to be as devastating as it was. Many people lost their lives or went missing.
